To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microvessel count and the expression of both vascular endothelial growth factors and basic fibroblast growth factor are increased in melanoma with metastasis at initial presentation.
(1) Microvessel density is increased in metastatic melanoma; (2) The expression of VEGFA and bFGF is increased in metastases; and (3) Microvessel densities are correlated with VEGF and with bFGF.
microvessel density as a marker of angiogenesis, as well as expression of VEGFA and bFGF, are correlated with melanoma metastasis and may be used for the prediction of melanoma progression.

the study of the correlation of microvessel count, VEGF and basic fibroblast growth factor expression in primary cutaneous malignant melanoma with metastasis.
